name: Can custom molding be installed on uneven or crooked walls?

mainEntity.name: Can custom molding be installed on uneven or crooked walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can add custom molding to crooked walls, but it requires specialized carpentry techniques like hand scribing, back-cutting, and coped corner joints. Standard 45-degree miter cuts pull apart on out-of-square corners, which are common in older homes across Denver and Greenwood Village. Carpenters cope inside corners so one profile fits over the contours of the other, allowing the joint to stay tight through minor framing movement. Where walls bow severely, HH Remodeling repairs or skims the drywall underneath and adds solid blocking behind the trim, ensuring the molding fastens securely without buckling.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, experienced carpenters use coped joints, scribing, and drywall adjustments to seat molding flush against uneven or out-of-square walls without separating.
